notes:
1. Shortened Duel Adventures to Adventures in every UI language, restoring a smaller main-menu highlight. Imported the updated Portuguese translation and retained newer missing entries.
2. Standard, Genesys and Rush banlists now update from the MDPro4 Cloudflare feed, keeping valid local lists when an update fails.
3. Added independent Deck Sync accounts with recovery keys and device linking. No email address is collected. Upload and sync decks from Settings; offline edits are preserved as conflict copies. Deleting a cloud deck keeps its local copy even when an interrupted sync later replays older changes. Removed the previous MyCard deck sync.
4. Fixed native tutorial command choices sending inspection actions as duel responses and delayed controller icons overwriting the active input prompts.
5. Puzzle guidance now remains available in chat history, uses normal locale translations and cannot carry queued hints into another attempt. Added missing WCS2006 victory hints.
6. Adventures now checks native-engine availability before launch and preserves host-compatible ordinary duels on Linux and macOS. Unsupported native tutorials and special starting states remain unavailable on those platforms.
7. Fixed empty Chain Resolve presentation and repeated resolve cues on intermediate links of longer chains.
8. Rebuilt the affected Android Switch stand, grave and field effects with their required mobile shader programs.
9. Update preparation and the desktop installer no longer probe unrelated disconnected drives when checking destination free space.
10. Optional MyCard news refresh deadlines keep valid cached news without reporting an expected cancellation as a service failure.
11. Fixed the sidebar hiding publicly activated hand-card artwork when replay hands are hidden. Other hidden hand cards remain concealed.
12. Restored three unavailable World Championship puzzles with their original-era card effects, scoped to those puzzles. Fixed Harpie cards loading the wrong effect scripts while preserving their shared card-name rules.
13. Added translated instructions for card effect, summon and finishing-attack showcases. Effect and summon demonstrations no longer impose an unrelated win-this-turn objective.
14. Synchronized repaired puzzles between Adventure data and Starter Pack, preserving organized folders and completion records without duplicate entries. Release tools now include the selected Starter Pack puzzles in full releases and patches while preserving unrelated personal puzzles.
15. Fixed settings, playback controls, duel log and chat remaining unavailable after the first game when spectating a LAN match.
16. Fixed opponent hand cards covering each other inconsistently with Android's depth-buffer precision, including at low resolutions.
17. Added Duel Expedition to Adventures: three starters, six duel stages, changing opponent lineups and six possible bosses. Choose one of six reward paths and Standard, Veteran or Expert difficulty, with three, two or one life. Track starter, path, difficulty, flawless and boss mastery. Runs save locally and remain protected during updates.
18. Fixed cancelled local duel startup retaining an idle host and blocking the next attempt. Cancellation now retires the connection and native host through their matching owners.
19. Added Combo Sheets to the Deck Editor submenu: read complete Chimera and Chaos Ritual examples, create multi-variant guides with card previews and annotated steps, and save drafts locally. Combo Sheets fills the screen and has a dedicated close button. Full combos open separately with a clear ending, grouped starting hands, endboards and follow-up resources, and numbered diagrams with arrows, alternatives and smoother action/location icons. Generic card slots show their requirements instead of unknown-card artwork. Customize the diagrams in the visual-flow editor. Use your Deck Sync account to publish, browse, search by archetype or custom tags, vote and manage your uploads. Publish directly from a local sheet or full combo. Community sheets display the uploader username and vote totals, including inside full combos; source-credit labels have been removed. Unpublish removes an upload while keeping local copies ready to edit and publish again. New sheets ask for a title before saving, older untitled drafts have a visible label, card captions stay aligned below long names, and long-text editing uses a centered writing panel with a proper multiline field.
20. Card Customization stays open while trying finishes, frames and name colors. Duel Appearance is hidden during duels.
21. Fixed the large card preview becoming unresponsive after leaving local duels. Closed windows now release their input ownership correctly.
22. Added direct Side Deck actions in Deck Editor and the large card preview. Use Shift + right-click on collection cards, Shift + middle-click on deck cards, or the displayed controller shortcut.
23. Fixed Engage's native search effect for extended-art Widow Anchor and Linkage, including replay playback.
24. Corrected field framing on wide Android displays and aligned mobile player profiles across asymmetric safe-area insets. Deck counts and the I-key info panels now follow camera and window resizing, without overlapping duplicate deck numbers. Mobile playback controls keep their original position when space allows and use a compact bottom-aligned layout when needed.
25. Added Remember Me for Evolution on Linux, storing the session token in the system keyring when available or a private local file. Passwords are not saved; expired sessions still require sign-in.
26. Added Your stats to Evolution's ranking panel and account menu. View your rank, wins, losses, win rate, rating, achievements and match history without appearing on the leaderboard.
27. New Duel Expeditions include a recovery camp, a risk/reward event and a merchant between duels. Earn supplies, gain reward rerolls or trade a life for an extra reward choice. Existing runs keep their original rules.
28. Duel Expeditions now retain the latest 20 finished runs with routes, rewards, results and final decks. Export completed expedition decks to your normal deck collection without replacing existing files.
29. Fixed saved card finishes disappearing from visible replay hands after a draw.
30. Fixed pre-release card updates failing on Android devices whose system temporary directory is not writable. Validation now uses application-owned storage and cleans up temporary database files.
31. Normal Android audio startup no longer tries to load an unavailable optional native sound plugin.
32. Added Progression Series to Adventures. Open packs in chronological OCG or TCG order, build decks from a separate saved collection in the normal Deck Editor and advance after your chosen number of duels. Customize sets, pack counts, rarity weights and duel rules. Winners choose bonus packs, cards from earlier sets or a rare discovery. Play against the AI or share a series file with a friend for LAN and supported Evolution rooms. Includes pack contents, native pack-opening animations and card results, a shared MDPRO4 pack design and complete set names. Opened cards save directly to the series pool, including when the animation is skipped.
33. Fixed Progression card results scrolling too far beyond the final cards and repeatedly reloading artwork while scrolling. Wheel movement now follows the card-row size and the selected menu scroll speed.
34. Release tools, installers and updates now protect saved Progression Series, including backups and exported series files, alongside tournament and expedition progress.
35. Progression Series can follow historical OCG or TCG banlists as packs advance, use a fixed list or keep N/A. Organizers can change the policy between duels and share the updated series. Deck checks and room admission enforce the selected list. Automatic banlist updates preserve local historical and custom lists absent from the live feed.
36. New Progression Series retain Neuron's printed rarity for each pulled card, including alternate rarities in the same pack. Added distinct rarity badges and matching available finishes in pack reveals, results and progression decks. Pack Contents lists the available printings; existing saves keep their original pulls.
37. Linux and macOS updates now extract and prepare rollback backups on the game's drive instead of the system temporary directory. Added disk-space checks and safer recovery when storage runs out; downloaded archives remain available after a failed installation for retry.
38. Windows updates now use the game's drive for temporary work and can remember another working folder. Added download and installation space checks, reduced duplicate writes when preparing and installing patches, and automatic cleanup of verified downloads after success. Both Windows helpers preserve rollback and keep failed-update downloads for retry.
39. Fixed printed Spell/Trap labels wrapping over card names and artwork in languages such as Portuguese. Long monster type labels and taller Thai text now fit their reserved row. Checked all eleven card locales.
40. Android player logs now include available OS exit history and low-memory, pause/resume and quit markers to help diagnose unexpected closures.
41. Timed-out connection attempts now close their pending sockets. Added timing and partial-packet diagnostics for online receive failures without logging card data.
42. Applied matching Portuguese translation corrections, organized the shared translation catalog by feature and removed replaced messages.
43. Evolution's Remember me option now works on Android using encrypted, app-private session storage protected by Android Keystore. Windows continues to use Credential Manager. Passwords are not saved; expired sessions still require sign-in, and signing out removes the saved session.
44. Fixed the mobile pack browser cover blocking pack selection. Search icons, placeholders and filter labels now fit their controls on both layouts.
45. Banlist updates now rebuild the file's header index to include retained historical and custom lists.
46. Evolution now shows how many players are searching in each supported matchmaking format. Matchmaking options let you wait for players only or choose when to allow an unrated practice bot.
47. Updated Evolution reconnect handling for servers that retain the same token throughout a match. Private-room password fields now show the available length after accounting for the room command.
48. Updated Rush artwork IDs and localized card catalogs, removed duplicate artwork variants, and refreshed normal and Over Rush illustrations using the supplied official references. Restored Bottomless Trap Hole's missing red eye glow. Corrected the swapped Princess Cosmos and Knight of the Hollowed Grounds artworks and the Silver Belfry Battery Bastion prize-art assignment. Added Grave Shadow's black Overframe and preserved separate Transam Linac and Armor Nova alternate artworks.
49. Added the available prerelease cards and artwork variants from Jointech of Passion and Limited Pack Another Style Edition to the main Rush card collection, with matching card effects and artwork mappings.
50. Replaced the temporary Sinner and Grave Shadow Rush scripts with their upstream versions and synchronized their card IDs, artwork mappings and localized catalogs.
51. Vertical card selection now fits the available screen height at larger UI scales, keeping the header, view controls and confirmation buttons reachable.
52. Deck screens now open at their final size, preventing a brief shrinking effect on ultrawide displays.
53. Windows room links now accept the slash added by browsers after join, allowing links to reach the requested room.
54. Rebuilt the remaining affected Switch stand, grave, field and mate shader programs for Android, Linux and macOS. Fixed AvatarStand_u046 losing its portal geometry after a few seconds and restored depth-dependent effects in individual accessory previews.
55. Added Complete all Solo Gates to the Solo Gates header. Confirm to mark installed gate missions complete and unlock their paths while retaining existing progress.
56. Fixed desktop attached-effect card lists failing to initialize their player indicator.
57. Fixed Demise, King of Armageddon repeatedly clearing its own cards and spending its last Life Points in adapted Solo battles. The opponent now checks whether the field wipe is worthwhile and avoids repeating it in the same turn.
58. The Duel Engine setting now controls offline AI duels, including Solo Gates, Link Evolution, campaigns, tournaments, Expeditions and Progression Series. Added native setups for all 201 ordinary Solo Gate duels. Incompatible scripts and rules now explain which engine is required instead of switching automatically. Native campaign results, surrender losses and retry restrictions follow their existing progression rules, and completed ordinary native Adventures can save replays. Online duels continue to use the server's engine.
59. Added advanced Master Duel CPU and starting-state options to Solo and Adventures. Keep the original setup or choose CPU values and flags, a fixed seed, turn order, Life Points, opening hands and shuffle behavior. Retries retain the chosen setup; guided tutorials keep their authored rules.
60. Fixed eight native tutorials rejecting their unchanged guides after the MDPro4 rename.
61. Fixed native replays rejecting valid loss or draw results because the finish reason was read as the duel result.
62. Native Free Solo now asks you to choose your player deck. Native pile actions use graphical card lists and localized names, recheck tutorial instructions before responding, and let you close inspection without cancelling the duel prompt.
63. Moving the mouse across a card-selection popup no longer replaces the card description you selected. Clicking a card and deliberate controller navigation still update it.
64. Added an optional Summon Chants setting under Appearance. The supplied Ra chant plays before the normal summon presentation and can be skipped with a click or Cancel; the setting starts disabled.
65. Rebuilt Rush prerelease packages with playable card data, scripts and available artwork. Completed missing German, Portuguese and other supported locale text and corrected source prompt imports, including Sengenjin. Rush prerelease cards appear in the Beta and Rush filters.
66. Desktop and mobile file imports now accept native Master Duel replays and reject corrupt recordings before replacing an existing file.
67. Public Deck Search now resolves the missing Original Artwork Collection cards, including installed prerelease versions, and rejects unavailable cards by exact identity. Restored native category/tag badges with scrolling and wrapped labels. Cover images now reuse small cached thumbnails, and recipe caching retains a complete result page.
68. Added verified staging of manually supplied Solo Adventure videos into prepared full releases and patches. Complete movie files are included without adding oversized media to the companion Git repository.
69. All three matching Maximum cards now glow when a Maximum Summon is available and can start it from hand. The center zone highlights for confirmation with a dedicated Maximum Summon prompt. A unique side pair is selected automatically; duplicate copies remain your choice. Fixed clicking the visible side cards on the field. Restored the three-card Xyz animation, with the center landing first and both sides rising from the hand. Fixed a particle initialization error in Xyz summon effects.
70. Related Cards now supports Rush Duel cards, including Maximum companions, Fusion materials and alternate artwork. Related-search fallback keeps standard and Rush formats separate and handles punctuation in card names correctly.
71. Added 116 missing original catalog covers and 1,146 custom covers using included-card artwork and complete product names; Japanese magazine issues are excluded. Added 214 matching digital Progression pack covers while preserving the approved Legend of Blue-Eyes White Dragon artwork.
72. Replaced the Progression Series menu thumbnail with digital artwork of Atem and the six priests in the Egyptian temple.
73. Kept direct Windows 1.0.3 and 1.0.3.1 updates compatible with the one-time updater recovery when a release upgrades its helper.
message: Small update steps start at 1.0.3. Windows and Android 1.0.1/1.0.2 installations need the current full installation; see the Workshop guide. Baseline installations retain their direct 1.0.4 patch. Reopen MDPro4 and check again after each staged update.

1. Rush Ritual monsters now use Ritual summon effects and voice categories instead of Fusion presentation.
2. Fixed clicks near overlapping Extra Deck and Side Deck card edges selecting the neighboring card in Deck Editor.
3. Fixed Genesys points appearing when opening Deck Editor with another card information mode selected.
4. Added Duel Links fields to Deck Appearance. Each deck can use a specific field, turn it off, or inherit the global setting.
5. Fixed Windows disk-space checks failing while preparing split updates and installing game resources in IL2CPP players.
6. Includes the restored Solo Adventures content and preserves existing settings, decks, progress and personal card choices.
